lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Role play or write a three-line script in which a student cannot open a heavy door while carrying books. Ask for help and then thank the helper.

FEEDBACK
Script: 'Excuse me, could you hold the door please? My arms are full.' Helper: 'Sure.' 'Thank you!' It has a polite opener, the need and thanks, and keeps the request short.

WATCH FOR
Believing that waiting silently will make others guess what you need. Adults and friends cannot read minds; clear words help.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Write and perform with a family member three role plays: asking for schoolwork help, finding a lost item, and telling an adult that something at the park felt unsafe. Include each part of a help request and note how your helper responded.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.

teach_steps.explain:
Role playing lets us practise asking for help before we need it. A good help request uses a calm voice, eye contact if that is comfortable, the helper's name, a short description of the problem and a thank-you. Listening to the answer and asking another question if you still do not understand is part of the skill. Role plays use made-up situations, and anyone may pass.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.

Now choose a different situation to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same PDHPE idea in a new place, game or situation, not a copy of the example. Review safety, fairness and inclusion.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.
